                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old woman goes to the genetic counseling clinic after having a child with Down syndrome. In the child, a trisomy 21 with translocation 21/21 inherited from the mother is identified. What would be the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in the future children of this woman?

                    ### Options
                    opa. The risk of recurrence will be 10-15%, as in the rest of translocations.
opb. 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
opc. The risk of recurrence will be very low (12%).
opd. The risk of recurrence will be 50%.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of a 21/21 translocation in the mother, all her gametes will contain two chromosome 21s. This means that any viable offspring will inherit an extra chromosome 21, resulting in Down syndrome. Therefore, the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in future children is 100%. This aligns with the consensus that a 21/21 translocation leads to all viable pregnancies resulting in trisomy 21, as there are no normal gametes produced. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, support the understanding that germ cells with altered genetic content can lead to conditions like trisomy and Down syndrome.
